trust_decision.summary: In restricted mode (restrict_to_base_dir=True), CodingTools._check_command decides whether an LLM-supplied command string may reach subprocess.run(shell=True): it uses a metacharacter blocklist, a basename allowlist and a path-token check, and python3 -c/-m/- slips past it to run arbitrary code.

landing_point.why: The summary names CodingTools.run_shell in coding.py. run_shell calls _check_command at coding.py:516, which is the only gate before shell=True.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API CodingTools.run_shell(command), registered as agent tool 'run_shell' (coding.py:185-186)

fix_sites.module_kind: toolkit validation helper (new interpreter inline-code check)
toolkit validation helper (CPython option parser emulation)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py:132 (enable_run_shell default True -> False, fix.diff:135-136); same file and class as the landing point, so it is not at distance

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fix's own docstring calls restricted mode 'harm-reduction heuristics, not a security sandbox' (fix.diff:120-127, 213-214), and the report is about python -c. A solver can argue that newline or '&' chaining and allowlisted tools that spawn programs (find -exec, git -c) are a different, accepted limitation.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Restricted mode must keep running a script file (python3 ok.py), an arg-taking option whose value is 'c' (python3 -W c ok.py), versioned or absolute interpreter paths for scripts, and all other allowlisted commands. Blocking python entirely, or blocking any token containing 'c'/'m', breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: clustered short options before c, e.g. -Ic
python / python3 / python3.12 / absolute path, matched by basename prefix
-W/-X/-Q value consumes the rest of its token (not code-exec)
option parsing stops at the first positional (script path)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Newline or single '&' used as a command separator: neither is in _DANGEROUS_PATTERNS, shlex.split treats newline as whitespace, so only the first command is checked against the allowlist while the shell runs every line or background job.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The blocklist looks complete for chaining ('&&', ';', '|'), and the report only covers interpreter flags.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same function as the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: find (allowlisted) with -exec/-execdir and a '+' terminator runs any program past the allowlist without needing the blocked ';'.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: find is a legitimate exploration command, and the fix scoped code-exec to interpreters ('python' prefix only, fix.diff:167).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: git (allowlisted) with -c config overrides (e.g. a pager, ssh-command or '!' alias value) runs any program.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: git is explicitly intended for agents, and config flags start with '-' so they look like plain options (coding.py:288-289).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pytest -p <module> and pip install of a local path load or execute arbitrary Python, the same as the blocked python -m.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Running tests and installing packages are documented core uses (coding.py:79-80).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Allowlist identity is the basename only, so ./python3 or any path ending in an allowlisted name passes; token 0 is exempt from the path check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Full-path commands are a tested legitimate behaviour (test_coding_tools.py:687-699).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Path check differential: '~/...' and '$HOME/...' tokens resolve under base_dir in Python but the shell expands them outside it; '--opt=/abs' tokens are skipped as flags.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is path confinement, not code execution, so a solver can call it a neighbouring property.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A restricted-mode allowlist on Workspace.run_command (argv list, no shell) that reuses the same basename and interpreter check, which a list-shaped input could bypass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer could plausibly port CodingTools' restricted mode to the second command-running toolkit in another file, giving a list-input shape and a real second implementation at distance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An allowed_commands gate on ShellTools.run_shell_command(args) that checks args[0] only.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ShellTools is the older shell toolkit, and a shared allowlist helper would naturally be added there too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An async arun_shell variant (asyncio subprocess) that skips or duplicates _check_command.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Workspace already ships async siblings via to_thread (workspace.py:1051-1063), so an async CodingTools path is a natural addition.

O9_family: OS command injection / allowlist bypass via an allowlisted interpreter (CWE-77/78)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject a literal ' -c ' token after python/python3 (or drop python from the allowlist), missing attached and clustered forms, -m, stdin, and the newline/'&' and find/git exec routes.

out_of_scope_notes: CodingTools.grep appends the pattern without '--' (libs/agno/agno/tools/coding.py:601-610), so a pattern starting with '-' is read as a grep option; this is a different tool and CWE-88, not pursued.
PythonTools (libs/agno/agno/tools/python.py) is documented as having no sandbox (commit 0d0db98d9); not pursued.
